title: Choosing new words through changing feelings

captions.physics: Discussing the current form of consent
captions.energy: Releasing an exhausted way of promising
captions.emotions: Experiencing change after a renewed reply

meaning: You can renew a familiar promise together while leaving room for changing emotional responses to a new way of talking.
text: A changed promise does not always feel familiar immediately. The Lovers in the physical position of Vishuddha discuss consent to a present conversational form while preserving both people’s choice. Death in energy supports readiness to release an exhausted way of giving your word and renew it honestly. The Wheel of Fortune in emotions makes the response changeable. New terms can first relieve and later bring regret. Conditions and feelings can both be discussed without making one successful reply settle every inward question connected with the earlier promise.

For example, you reconsider a promise to recount the whole day in detail every evening. One wants less compulsory reporting; the other wants to preserve a moment of meeting. **New words can remain shared through a changing feeling.** A brief account of what matters can be chosen, leaving the rest free. Sometimes that form is enough; sometimes more is wanted. A separate request gives the present wish words without declaring earlier consent mistaken.

The difficulty is turning each wave of regret into another choice of the entire conversational arrangement. Terms change before they become understandable. Feeling deserves attention without automatically directing a permanent promise. Naming today’s request preserves flexibility; genuinely new terms can be accepted when both people want to discuss and confirm them.
